questions.q: What is packet rate in ELRS?
questions.explain: More packets means lower latency, but worse sensitivity and range.

questions.q: For a long-range wing over forest, the better choice is…
questions.explain: The longer wavelength bends around obstacles, and a low packet rate gives you sensitivity margin.

questions.q: Telem ratio 1:128 at 500 Hz gives telemetry once every…

options: The basis of the hopping pattern
The encryption password for the control link
questions.explain: Not a secret and not protection: a unique phrase is needed so you don't collide with your neighbors.

questions.q: LQ 100% with RSSI at the sensitivity threshold means…
options: Everything is great: all packets get through
The edge of the link with no margin
questions.explain: LQ is whether the packets get through, RSSI is how much margin is left. You need both.

questions.q: RXLOSS when turning with the back toward the pilot. Likely cause?
options: The antenna is shadowed by the frame
Low packet rate and a weak radio battery
Interference from the 5.8 GHz video transmitter
questions.explain: Antenna shadowing is a classic. Move it out and orient it.

questions.q: Sensitivity of ELRS 2.4 GHz at 250 Hz:
Telemetry ratio 1:128 at 250 Hz gives a telemetry interval of:
Long-range flight, ELRS 2.4 GHz in 250 Hz mode. Telemetry at the edge of the zone:
questions.fragment:
RSSI1 -104 dBm  RSSI2 -106 dBm  LQ 71%  SNR -2 dB
sensitivity of 250 Hz mode ≈ -108 dBm
options: A 2–4 dB margin — the link is on the verge of failsafe: lower the packet rate or turn back
LQ 71 % is normal for a long-range flight; failsafe only happens at LQ below 10 %
SNR -2 dB means a faulty receiver: on a working one it's always positive
You need to raise the packet rate to 500 Hz — that will increase receiver sensitivity
questions.explain: The margin is counted from the mode's sensitivity; 500 Hz is even less sensitive.
